genuine.stem: In a series combination of resistors, what can you say about the current?
genuine.explanation: In a series combination the ammeter reading is the same wherever it is placed, so the same current flows through each resistor.

citations.section: 11.6 Resistance of a System of Resistors

options: The current is different in each resistor
The current is the same in every part of the circuit
The current is largest in the biggest resistor
The current becomes zero after the first resistor
genuine.answer: The current is the same in every part of the circuit

genuine.stem: Three resistors are joined in parallel and the potential difference across the combination is V. What is the potential difference across each resistor?
genuine.explanation: In a parallel combination the potential difference across each resistor is the same and equals V, the potential difference across the combination.

citations.section: 11.6 Resistance of a System of Resistors > 11.6.2 Resistors in Parallel

options: V
3V
It is different for each resistor

genuine.stem: An electric lamp of resistance 20 ohm and a conductor of resistance 4 ohm are connected in series to a 6 V battery. Find the total resistance of the circuit.
genuine.explanation: In series the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances, so Rs = 20 + 4 = 24 ohm.

citations.section: 11.6 Resistance of a System of Resistors > 11.6.1 Resistors in Series

genuine.stem: An electric lamp of resistance 20 ohm and a conductor of resistance 4 ohm are connected in series to a 6 V battery. Find the current through the circuit.
genuine.explanation: The total resistance is 24 ohm, and by Ohm's law I = V/Rs = 6/24 = 0.25 A.

citations.section: 11.6 Resistance of a System of Resistors > 11.6.1 Resistors in Series

genuine.stem: Which of these is needed for autotrophic nutrition?
genuine.explanation: Autotrophs take in carbon dioxide and water and convert them into carbohydrates using sunlight and chlorophyll.
options: Only carbon dioxide
Carbon dioxide and water
Only chlorophyll
Only sunlight

genuine.stem: In the starch test, why is the variegated leaf dipped in alcohol after boiling it in water?
genuine.explanation: The leaf is immersed in alcohol so that the green colour (chlorophyll) is removed, which helps to see the starch test result clearly.
options: To absorb carbon dioxide
To remove the green colour of the leaf
To add starch to the leaf
To open the stomatal pores
genuine.answer: To remove the green colour of the leaf

genuine.stem: The opening and closing of the stomatal pore is controlled by the guard cells. When does the pore open?
genuine.explanation: The guard cells swell when water flows into them, and this makes the stomatal pore open.
options: When the leaf is kept in a dark room
When the guard cells shrink
When the guard cells swell with water
When potassium hydroxide absorbs carbon dioxide
genuine.answer: When the guard cells swell with water
